title: Epigenetic-metabolic regulation of macrophage pyroptosis by FTO-m6A-NLRP3 axis: insights from multi-omics analysis
abstract: Sepsis, a severe illness marked by immune dysregulation and widespread inflammation, involves macrophage pyroptosis as a key player. This study explores the impact of RNA N6-methyladenosine (m 6 A) modification and investigates whether fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO)-mediated demethylation influences macrophage pyroptosis by modulating NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation. The research aims to unravel the workings of the FTO-m 6 A-NLRP3 pathway in macrophage pyroptosis and assess the therapeutic potential of targeted intervention using biomimetic nanovesicles. Results:By developing CD11b/CD206 dual-ligand modified macrophage-derived small extracellular vesicle (sEV)-biomimetic nanovesicles loaded with FB23-2, an FTO inhibitor (FB23-2-loaded Dual-Vesicles) and employing various molecular techniques, including MeRIP-qPCR, WB, scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and metabolomics, the study delves into the mechanism by which FTO-regulated m 6 A modification impacts NLRP3 inflammasome and inflammatory metabolic pathways. Findings reveal upregulated FTO levels in septic macrophages, reduced m 6 A modification levels, and increased expression of NLRP3 and interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β). Treatment with an FTO inhibitor increased m6A modification of Il1b mRNA, reduced IL-1β expression, and attenuated NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis-associated changes. FB23-2-loaded Dual-Vesicles showed enhanced macrophage uptake and pulmonary enrichment, improved 7-day survival, and reduced inflammatory injury in murine models. Conclusions: These findings support further evaluation of the FTO-m6A-NLRP3-pyroptosis regulatory network as a targeted epigenetic intervention strategy in sepsis and related inflammatory diseases.

title: Ultrasound-triggered cascade-targeted nanoplatform enables controllable precision delivery for enhanced acute kidney injury therapy
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) suffers from limited therapeutic efficacy largely owing to insufficient targeted accumulation and uncontrollable on-demand delivery of conventional therapeutics. To overcome these drug delivery bottlenecks, we develop an ultrasound-triggered cascade-targeted nanoplatform (LSMND). Different from conventional static nanocarriers with fixed particle sizes, LSMND achieves controllable in situ particle remodeling and deep renal delivery through ultrasound-activated perfluoropentane (PFP) liquid-gas phase transition. Surface-functionalized LTH peptides further endow LSMND with active targeting ability, enabling precise enrichment in injured proximal tubules. The oxidative microenvironment induces the cleavage of ROS-responsive thioketal (TK) linkages, triggering programmed disassembly of LSMND and spatiotemporal co-delivery of SS31 and MCC950. The released SS31 preserves mitochondrial structural integrity and ameliorates mitochondrial bioenergetics, thereby restricting mtDNA leakage and suppressing Z-DNA binding protein 1 ( Zbp1 )-associated inflammatory activation. MCC950 suppresses the NLRP3 inflammatory cascade, synergistically potentially alleviates the detrimental metabolic-inflammatory loop. Integrated proteotranscriptomic analyses verify that LSMND alleviates upstream mitochondrial stress and blocks aberrant pro-inflammatory activation. In a murine renal ischemia-reperfusion injury model, LSMND substantially alleviates tubular necrosis and promotes renal functional recovery. This US-activated cascade-targeted nanoplatform provides a controllable and precise therapeutic strategy for AKI treatment.

title: Epitope and immunological basis for superior immunogenicity of henipavirus glycoprotein HeV.G over NiV.G in mRNA vaccines
abstract: Nipah (NiV) and Hendra (HeV) viruses are highly lethal zoonotic Henipaviruses with pandemic potential, for which no licensed vaccines exist. The surface glycoprotein (G) is the primary target of neutralizing antibodies, yet a systematic comparison of the immunogenicity of NiV.G and HeV.G has been lacking. Here, we engineered mRNA vaccines encoding the full-length G proteins of NiV and HeV. In Syrian hamsters, while both vaccines conferred homologous protection, only HeV.G vaccination at a lower dose (5 µg) provided complete cross-protection against lethal NiV challenge. Comparative immune profiling revealed that HeV.G vaccination induced significantly higher neutralizing antibody titers, which correlated with robust germinal center B cell expansion and a stronger CD4 + T follicular helper (Tfh) cell response, despite equivalent B cell activation. Epitope mapping uncovered a structurally conserved yet immunologically divergent MHC class II-restricted peptide (YIAITKVER) in HeV.G with superior predicted binding affinity, providing a mechanistic basis for the enhanced T cell help. Our work establishes HeV.G as a superior vaccine immunogen due to its distinct epitope repertoire and underscores the critical role of CD4 + T cell help in driving cross-protective B cell immunity. We further developed a bivalent vaccine Gmix, which induced balanced antibody and cellular immune responses against both G proteins, thereby confirming the value of multivalent vaccines in broadening immune coverage. Collectively, this study defines HeV.G as the preferred antigen for pan-henipavirus vaccine development and offers a framework for rational antigen selection against future viral threats.

title: Therapy-induced senescence in cancer: from detection to intervention
abstract: Therapy-induced senescence (TIS) has emerged as an important contributor to treatment resistance and poor prognosis in clinical cancer therapy. Senescence initially acts as a tumor-suppressive mechanism by enforcing stable cell-cycle arrest, while the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) promotes the formation of pro-tumorigenic microenvironment, ultimately leading to therapeutic resistance and tumor relapse. Precise detection and targeted elimination of TIS have emerged as an important focus in cancer treatment. In this review, we first summarize tumor-specific fluorescent probes for senescence detection, including enzyme-responsive, non-enzymatic, dual-responsive, and theranostic platforms. We further discuss current senolytic approaches, including classical Bcl-2 family inhibitors, dasatinib-quercetin combinations, and emerging senolytic strategies. In addition, we summarize the cutting-edge senolytic regimens that synergize with chemotherapy, radiotherapy, photothermal therapy, and immunotherapy. Finally, we highlight the key challenges and future perspectives for clinical translation and application.

title: CRISPR screening identifies TWIST1 as a ferroptosis driver in CKD progression
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) lacks effective therapeutic interventions targeting its fundamental pathological mechanisms. TWIST1 is a basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor that is a critical regulator in kidney fibrosis pathogenesis. We used genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screening to delineate the role of TWIST1 in ferroptosis and explored the impact of an inflammation-responsive lipid nanoparticle (LTH-TK-LNP, a Kim-1-targeted reactive oxygen species-responsive lipid nanoparticle platform that releases si-RNA targeting TWIST1 specifically in inflamed renal tissue) in mouse models of CKD. CRISPR-Cas9 screening showed that TWIST1 is significantly upregulated under hypoxic conditions and drives ferroptosis by suppressing oxidative phosphorylation, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction, lipid peroxidation, and accumulation of reactive oxygen species. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated superior targeting of LTH-TK-LNP to injured kidneys compared to unmodified nanoparticles. In CKD mouse models, LTH-TK-LNP treatment significantly reduced TWIST1 expression, attenuated tubular damage and interstitial fibrosis, suppressed lipid peroxidation and the expression of inflammatory cytokines, and preserved mitochondrial integrity. Safety assessments revealed no evidence of hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity over a 14-day observation period. This study identifies TWIST1 as a master regulator connecting metabolic dysfunction to ferroptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells during CKD progression. Furthermore, we reveal the significant therapeutic potential of targeting TWIST1 and lay the preclinical foundation for kidney-targeted delivery strategies. Graphical Abstract. Schematic illustration of the LTH-TK-LNP nanoplatform for targeted si-TWIST1 delivery to treat chronic kidney disease. LTH-TK-LNPs are assembled via co-incubation and extrusion using a ROS-responsive, Kim-1-targeting lipid (DSPE-TK-PEG-LTHVVWL) and standard lipid components. Upon intravenous injection, the nanoparticles specifically accumulate in injured renal tubules. Release of si-TWIST1 silences TWIST1 expression, which restores oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial function. This metabolic reprogramming reduces ROS accumulation and lipid peroxidation, ultimately suppressing ferroptosis and attenuating renal fibrosis.

title: A MAM-targeted integrated atomic-precision MnSe janus nanozyme platform inhibits pyroptosis and ferroptosis for intervertebral disc degeneration therapy
abstract: Aberrant endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–mitochondria crosstalk at mitochondria-associated ER membranes (MAMs) drives oxidative stress, calcium dysregulation, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis in nucleus pulposus cells, accelerating intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). Nanozymes that mimic antioxidant enzymes and remodel the oxidative stress microenvironment are promising for IVDD treatment, but their efficacy is limited by low enzyme-like activity and poor targeting of MAMs. To address this, we developed a space-confined pyrolysis strategy to synthesize N/O co-doped hollow bamboo-like porous carbon nanotubes loaded with atomically Janus MnSe dual atoms, and functionalization with the MAM-targeting protein GRP75 and σ1R-regulator CGI1746 yielded GC-MnSe DA /BCNT, an integrated nanozyme platform for precise IVDD intervention. The hollow BCNT framework exposed atomically dispersed MnSe sites, while the MnSeN 5 O Janus active center optimizes Mn’s local electronic structure via Se-mediated p-d orbital hybridization, promoting electron transfer and lowering the reaction energy barrier, thereby boosting SOD-, CAT-, and GPx-like activities. This platform exhibited high biosafety and potent multi-enzyme antioxidant activity, enabling efficient ROS scavenging and inhibition of lipid peroxidation. Importantly, it restored the integrity of MAMs and mitochondrial function, maintained Ca 2 ⁺ homeostasis, and suppressed NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis and ferroptosis, thereby delaying IVDD progression. This work provides an efficient, safe, and precise new strategy for the treatment of degenerative and inflammatory diseases.

title: Biosynthetic DNA origami nanostructures: harnessing E. coli-phage systems as nanofactories
abstract: DNA origami nanostructures (DONs) serve as versatile nanocarriers with promising application potential, but high production cost and low yield limit their development. The biosynthetic approach based on the Escherichia coli ( E. coli )-phage system offers an effective route for the low-cost, scalable fabrication of DONs. This approach relies on the biosynthetic production of single-stranded DNA via in vivo rolling circle replication, offering advantages of nucleic acid sequence fidelity and length scalability. This review summarizes recent advances in the biosynthesis of DONs using the E. coli -phage system, with a focus on biosynthetic strategies, and briefly introduces the production of functionalized DONs. Furthermore, we provide a comprehensive overview of the entire biosynthetic workflow, and discuss the advantages and challenges of the biosynthetic approach in depth. This review aims to provide insights for researchers in related fields and to facilitate the development of DNA origami technology.

title: Enteric-gated nano–probiotic living nanozyme for gut-directed redox–mitochondrial protection in cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury
abstract: Oral nano-biohybrid therapeutics provide opportunities for gut–organ axis intervention, but gastrointestinal transit often compromises both probiotic viability and nanozyme activity. Here, we developed CeO 2 @LP@EL, an enteric-gated nano–probiotic living nanozyme constructed by decorating cerium oxide nanozymes onto viable Lactobacillus paracasei and enclosing the hybrid within an EL100-55 enteric layer. This hierarchical architecture preserved hybrid integrity, viable bacterial survival, redox-protective activity, and epithelial adhesion after simulated gastrointestinal processing. In intestinal epithelial cells, CeO 2 @LP@EL reduced oxidative stress and supported antioxidant homeostasis. In cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury, oral CeO 2 @LP@EL attenuated renal dysfunction and tubular damage, accompanied by intestinal barrier repair, reduced endotoxemia and inflammation, oxidative stress suppression, gut microbiota remodeling, mitochondrial preservation, and recovery-associated renal transcriptional changes. These findings identify enteric gating as a practical nano-biohybrid design principle for coordinating probiotic viability and nanozyme-associated redox regulation in gut-directed renoprotection. CeO 2 @LP@EL integrates enteric gating, nanoceria redox buffering, and probiotic gut regulation to enable gut-directed renoprotection against cisplatin-induced AKI.

title: Multimodal folate receptor-targeted liposomes enable photo-chemo-antibiotic synergy for peritoneal cancer therapy
abstract: The complex and heterogeneous nature of cancer presents significant challenges to effective treatment. Because no single therapy can overcome this complex challenge, rational combination strategies that concurrently target tumor survival pathways and engage non-overlapping mechanisms hold the greatest promise. We previously demonstrated that photodynamic priming and repurposing of the antibiotic minocycline can enhance chemotherapy efficacy in vivo . However, these approaches lack cancer selectivity and require multiple administrations. To address these limitations, we developed a single, stable, folate receptor-targeted liposomal formulation that co-packages irinotecan and minocycline within the aqueous core and incorporates the photosensitizer lipid-anchored benzoporphyrin derivative (BPD) within the lipid bilayer. This unique fol ate receptor-targeted l iposome containing i rinotecan, mi nocycline, and lipid-anchored B PD (FOLIMIB) nanoformulation enhances multidrug delivery to cancer cells, significantly downregulating both topoisomerase 1 (Top1) and tyrosyl-DNA phosphodiesterase 1 (Tdp1), thereby increasing DNA damage in 2D and 3D ovarian cancer models. Furthermore, in a peritoneal metastases mouse model, FOLIMIB achieved higher intratumoral drug accumulation compared with non-targeted l iposome containing i rinotecan, mi nocycline, and lipid-anchored B PD (LIMIB) and demonstrated a light dose-dependent photodynamic enhancement of survival outcomes. This multimodal platform shows promise for enhancing Top1 inhibitor-based chemotherapy by targeting DNA damage and DNA repair pathways, warranting further mechanistic investigation and evaluation under multi-cycle dosing regimens to achieve sustained therapeutic benefit and prolonged animal survival.

title: A biomimetic dual-targeting nanoplatform enhancing pyroptosis and chemosensitization for precision therapy of diffuse large b-cell lymphoma
abstract: Abstract Objective To elucidate the role of SHP-2 in regulating pyroptosis through the TXNIP‑NLRP3 inflammasome axis in diffuse large B‑cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and safety of a SHP099‑loaded B‑cell membrane–CD20 aptamer dual‑targeting biomimetic nanoplatform (SHP099@Bmem‑AptCD20). Methods SHP-2 was knocked down using shRNA. Pyroptosis was assessed by Western blot, immunofluorescence, transmission electron microscopy, Annexin V/PI staining, FAM-FLICA caspase-1 assays, and apoptosis-marker analysis. Protein interactions were analyzed by co-immunoprecipitation. The nanoplatform was characterized for particle size, membrane orientation, AptCD20 density, serum stability, drug release, cellular uptake, CD20-dependent specificity, and normal B-cell safety. Pharmacokinetics, tissue distribution, antitumor activity, and preliminary safety were evaluated in NOD/SCID xenograft models. Results SHP-2 downregulation suppressed proliferation and invasion while inducing pyroptosis hallmarks, including GSDMD-N and cleaved caspase-1 upregulation and increased LDH, IL-1β, and IL-18. Mechanistically, SHP-2 interacted with TXNIP and limited TXNIP-NLRP3 association, whereas NLRP3 inhibition or TXNIP interference attenuated the downstream pyroptotic response. SHP-2 inhibition enhanced doxorubicin-induced pyroptosis and reduced the IC50. The SHP099@Bmem-AptCD20 nanoparticles (approximately 145 nm, PDI < 0.2) retained B-cell membrane proteins, maintained a predominantly right-side-out membrane orientation, displayed stable AptCD20 retention in serum, and showed enhanced CD20-dependent uptake. Pharmacokinetic and tissue distribution analyses indicated prolonged systemic exposure and increased tumor SHP099 accumulation, while apoptosis-marker assays supported pyroptosis-dominant mixed cell death. Normal B-cell assays and organ safety analyses indicated limited short-term toxicity under the tested conditions. Conclusion SHP-2 functions as a pyroptosis suppressor by modulating the TXNIP-NLRP3 axis in DLBCL. The SHP099@Bmem-AptCD20 nanoplatform improves SHP099 delivery, supports CD20-dependent tumor targeting, and provides a rationale for further preclinical development of pyroptosis-based combination therapy.

title: Carrier-free supramolecular co-assembly enables oxygen-economizing photodynamic therapy via mitochondrial respiration suppression
abstract: Abstract Hypoxia within the tumor microenvironment severely compromises the therapeutic efficacy of photodynamic therapy (PDT) by limiting oxygen-dependent reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Although extensive efforts have been devoted to oxygen-supplementation strategies, most existing approaches provide only transient hypoxia relief and are hindered by limited oxygen-loading capacity, premature oxygen leakage, and insufficient catalytic efficiency. Herein, we report a carrier-free self-assembly nanodrug (BBR-Ce6 NPs) that enhances PDT through a durable oxygen-economizing strategy by reducing mitochondrial oxygen consumption rather than directly supplying oxygen. The nanodrug is composed of the mitochondria-targeting oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) inhibitor berberine (BBR) and the clinically used photosensitizer chlorin e6 (Ce6), which spontaneously co-assemble via synergistic π-π stacking and hydrogen-bonding interactions to form stable nanoparticles with high drug-loading efficiency. Benefiting from reversible noncovalent interactions, BBR-Ce6 NPs gradually disassemble within the mildly acidic tumor microenvironment, enabling tumor-responsive drug release. Following cellular internalization, BBR preferentially accumulates in mitochondria and inhibits mitochondrial complex I activity, thereby suppressing OXPHOS, reducing cellular oxygen consumption, and durably alleviating tumor hypoxia. This oxygen-sparing effect markedly enhances Ce6-mediated ROS generation and significantly improves PDT efficacy both in vitro and in vivo. In addition, the carrier-free formulation minimizes excipient-associated toxicity while simplifying nanoparticle fabrication. Collectively, this study establishes a safe and sustained hypoxia-relief strategy for enhancing PDT efficacy and offers a versatile nanoplatform for combining natural mitochondrial modulators with photosensitizers to overcome hypoxia-associated resistance of PDT in cancer treatment.

title: Migrasomes derived from Piezo1-activated mesenchymal stem cells with osteogenic and angiogenic activities alleviate osteoporosis: a novel therapeutic agent for bone regeneration
abstract: Osteoporosis is characterized by decreased bone mass and degraded bone microstructure. Piezo1, a mechanosensitive ion channel, has been demonstrated to be a key molecule mediating the transduction of mechanical stimuli into biological signals. Piezo1 activation has been shown to alleviate osteoporosis, but its underlying regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely clarified. Migrasomes secreted by migrating cells carry spatial positional information and play a crucial role in regulating intercellular communication. This study reveals that migrasomes possess the potential function of alleviating osteoporosis through Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis. In vivo experimental results indicate that Yoda1, a Piezo1-specific agonist, significantly promotes the secretion of migrasomes by mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). This suggests that Piezo1-mediated migrasomes formation may be a crucial mechanism by which Yoda1 ameliorates osteoporosis. We further found that bone marrow MSCs (BMSCs) could secrete migrasomes. Moreover, migrasomes derived from Yoda1-pretreated BMSCs (Mig-Yoda1) are enriched with multiple functional proteins. Experiments demonstrate that Mig-Yoda1 significantly enhance osteogenesis and angiogenesis. Mechanistically, Mig-Yoda1 promotes osteogenesis by maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis and activating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Finally, Mig-Yoda1 effectively alleviate bone loss in osteoporotic mice. In summary, this study reveals a regulatory association between Piezo1 and migrasomes biogenesis, while also confirming the potential therapeutic value of Mig-Yoda1 with integrated spatiotemporal multidimensional information as a cell-free therapeutic agent for osteoporosis. The study proposes a new approach and experimental evidence for the clinical treatment of osteoporosis.

title: Correction: Oral administration of probiotic spore ghosts for efficient attenuation of radiation-induced intestinal injury
Ultrasound-activated hollow FeOOH/MnO2 nanocatalysts for tumor barrier disruption and synergistic sonodynamic-ferroptosis therapy
abstract: Breast cancer treatment is often hindered by dense tumor stromal and extracellular matrix barriers, which limit the efficacy of conventional therapies. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) has emerged as a promising noninvasive strategy to overcome these barriers, while its efficacy is often limited by insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Here, a rationally designed sonocatalytic nanoplatform composed of hollow FeOOH-modified MnO 2 nanoparticles (HFM) was synthesized for the SDT of breast cancer. First, FeOOH modification and ate the electronic band structure of HFM, producing a more negative conduction band that facilitates ultrasound (US)-triggered electron transfer and boosts ROS production. Additionally, the Mn component enables sonocatalytic glutathione (GSH) depletion, which, when combined with Fe-mediated iron overload, amplifies oxidative stress and triggers ferroptosis. Simultaneously, US-induced cavitation transiently disrupts tumor interstitial and extracellular matrix barriers, enhancing deep intratumoral penetration of HFM and further potentiating its therapeutic efficacy. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate that US-activated HFM induces ferroptosis-related gene regulation, deep tumor penetration, and robust antitumor efficacy with minimal systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work presents a multifunctional sonosensitizer with enhanced catalytic activity, barrier-penetrating capability, and ferroptosis-inducing potential, offering a promising strategy for US-augmented breast cancer therapy.

title: Metal-site engineering in Prussian blue analogues tunes catalytic selectivity for radiation-induced heart disease therapy
abstract: Nanozymes with multi-enzyme activity offer substantial potential for treating diseases associated with reactive oxygen species (ROS). However, poor catalytic selectivity and uncontrolled reactivity often impair their therapeutic efficacy in diseased tissues and may even exacerbate oxidative damage. Here, we present a metal-site engineering strategy in Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) to achieve selective antioxidant catalysis. Through systematic screening of five PBAs, we identified ZnCu-PBA as an optimal candidate, which exhibited markedly enhanced catalase (CAT)-like activity while effectively suppressed peroxidase (POD)-like activity. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that Zn incorporation tuned the electronic structure of Cu active sites, shifting the catalytic preference from •OH generation toward O 2 production. ZnCu-PBA additionally displayed intrinsic superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activity. Owing to its CAT- and SOD-like activities, ZnCu-PBA effectively eliminated excess ROS, thereby attenuating X-ray-induced injury in H9C2 cells in vitro. Moreover, ZnCu-PBA exhibited exceptional cardioprotective effects in vivo against X-ray-induced cardiac injury. Mechanistically, it scavenged excessive ROS and alleviated oxidative stress, thereby attenuating the DNA damage response and suppressing the p53-p21 signaling and NF-κB-mediated pro-inflammatory signaling, ultimately mitigating cardiac dysfunction and myocardial fibrosis. This study demonstrates the therapeutic potential of selective antioxidant nanozymes for radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD) and provides a rational strategy for regulating nanozyme catalytic selectivity.

title: HA-modified lipid nanoparticles delivering ASO-Hotair attenuate macrophage-driven inflammation in sepsis-associated acute lung injury
abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SA-ALI) is a life-threatening condition driven by macrophage-mediated inflammation and endothelial injury, yet effective targeted therapies remain lacking. ADAM17, a key sheddase regulating TNF-α release and NF-κB activation, amplifies inflammatory responses. Whether targeting HOTAIR can modulate ADAM17-driven macrophage inflammation and enable nanotherapy in SA-ALI remains unknown. We analyzed HOTAIR and ADAM17 expression in SA-ALI patients and CLP-induced SA-ALI mice. HA-modified MC3 lipid nanoparticles delivering Hotair-targeted antisense oligonucleotide (ASO-Hotair) were developed to evaluate targeting efficiency, safety, and therapeutic efficacy for SA-ALI. Mechanistic studies were performed in LPS-stimulated bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) and RAW264.7 macrophages and Hotair -knockout SA-ALI mice. HOTAIR and ADAM17 were significantly upregulated in SA-ALI patients and mice, and correlated with sepsis severity and inflammatory markers. HA-modified MC3-LNPs exhibited high encapsulation efficiency, stability, and biocompatibility, and enhanced uptake by pulmonary macrophages, with preferential lung accumulation in septic mice. MC3-LNPs-HA@ASO-Hotair effectively silenced Hotair, reduced ADAM17 levels, inhibited NF-κB activation, suppressed M1-like macrophage polarization in BMDMs and RAW264.7 macrophages, and attenuated macrophage-mediated endothelial injury in vitro. In vivo, treatment reduced macrophage infiltration, attenuated lung injury, decreased inflammatory mediators, and improved survival, with efficacy comparable to that of Hotair deficiency and no additional benefit in Hotair -knockout mice. Mechanistically, HOTAIR regulated ADAM17 expression, at least partly through miR-326, thereby promoting downstream NF-κB activation. Consistently, Hotair deficiency markedly reduced proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and endothelial injury markers, suppressed TNF-α/NF-κB signaling, alleviated lung injury, and improved survival in septic mice. Preferential delivery of MC3-LNPs-HA@ASO-Hotair to pulmonary macrophages enables Hotair silencing, attenuates ADAM17-driven macrophage inflammation, and improves survival in SA-ALI, providing a mechanistic and preclinical framework for lncRNA-targeted nanotherapy in sepsis.

title: Synergistic nanotheranostic platform for fluorescence/magnetic resonance bimodal imaging-guided near infrared photoimmuno-chemodynamic thermal targeting therapy
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) photoimmunotherapy (PIT) is a promising cancer treatment strategy involving antibody–photoabsorber conjugates. However, the imaging depth and photobleaching susceptibility of the IR700 fluorescence used for treatment monitoring are limited, and antigen heterogeneity within tumors compromises the efficacy of strictly antigen-restricted therapies. We developed a synergistic nanotheranostic platform that integrates NIR-PIT, photothermal therapy, and chemodynamic therapy (CDT) into a single MRI-visible agent (NIR-PICT 3 ). To achieve NIR-PICT 3 , conjugation of mAb–IRDye700DX (mAb-IR700) to dextran-coated superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (nanomag-D-spio) yielded nanomag-D-spio-mAb-IR700, enabling dual imaging (IR700 fluorescence/MRI) and targeted cytotoxicity upon 690-nm irradiation. The conjugate retained antigen selectivity, exhibited activatable NIR fluorescence after cellular uptake, generated negative T1- and T2-weighted MRI contrast, and demonstrated robust, cycle-enhanced photothermal performance. Iron-mediated redox catalysis promoted ·OH generation, supporting CDT. In vivo, systemic administration led to marked tumor accumulation, as confirmed by multimodal analyses. Repeated light dosing exploited the NIR-PIT–induced super-enhanced permeability and retention (SUPR) effect, enhancing nanoparticle retention, tumor heating, and therapeutic efficacy. In EGFR+ xenografts, NIR-PICT 3 achieved superior tumor regression and survival while inducing photothermal bystander effects in antigen-heterogeneous models. These results establish a modular, image-guided strategy for platform therapy to overcome monitoring depth limitations and antigen heterogeneity in solid tumor NIR-PIT.

title: ROS-responsive yeast microcapsule oral delivery system for targeted celastrol delivery and kidney stones treatment
abstract: Abstract Background Kidney stones are a common urological disease characterized by a cycle of calcium deposition and inflammation. Balancing macrophage polarization is a promising strategy for treatment. Celastrol (Cel) is an effective compound to treat kidney stones, but its oral use is limited by low bioavailability. Yeast microcapsule (YC) is a considerable candidate for oral drug delivery to improve bioavailability. Results An oral delivery system (HCeY) was developed using YC and hyperbranched poly(β-amino thioether ester) (HPBTEa). After oral dosing, the β-glucan on YC surface is recognized and transcytosed by intestinal M cells. The carriers are then internalized by macrophages and transported to renal inflammatory sites. At the site of the stones, high levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) trigger the cleavage of thioether bonds in HPBTEa to release Cel. HCeY breaks the “renal injury-stone formation” cycle through three mechanisms: achieving renal targeting via macrophage “hitchhiking”; inhibiting STAT1 to reduce M1 macrophage polarization; and scavenging ROS to relieve endoplasmic reticulum stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. Conclusions This study developed a promising YC-assisted formulation that could enhance the bioavailability and renal accumulation of Cel, establishing a theoretical basis for the future clinical application of YC-based drug delivery systems in kidney stone therapy.

title: Tetrahedral framework nucleic acids loaded with resveratrol and TNF-α aptamer for the treatment of peripheral joint lesions in ankylosing spondylitis
abstract: Abstract Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic systemic inflammatory disease affecting the spine, sacroiliac and peripheral joints, with TNF-α as a core pro-inflammatory cytokine. Macrophages, as major TNF-α producers, form a positive feedback loop that amplifies local inflammatory responses. The use of clinical TNF inhibitors such as infliximab is limited by their high cost and high recurrence rate. This study constructs a targeted nano-delivery system named RSV@tFNAs-TNFαapt, by conjugating TNF-α aptamer to tetrahedral DNA nanostructures and loading resveratrol, a natural polyphenol with potent anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and immunomodulatory activities. The nanosystem showed uniform morphology, good stability and high cell uptake efficiency. In vitro, it promotes M2 macrophage polarization, inhibits pro-inflammatory and tissue-destruction-related factors, and reduced ROS production in synovial fibroblasts. In an AS rat model, it improves motor function, relieves joint swelling, alleviates spinal inflammation and structural damage, and reduces the production of peripheral inflammatory factors. Histopathology results confirms less inflammatory cell infiltration and protected cartilage and bone structure. In summary, RSV@tFNAs-TNFαapt exerts significant targeted anti-inflammatory and joint-protective effects, providing a complementary therapeutic strategy for AS, especially for peripheral joint lesions.
