title: Extracellular vesicle-derived circ6853 drives vascular remodeling and serves as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for gastric cancer
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC), a leading global malignancy, urgently requires the discovery of novel diagnostic and therapeutic targets. The roles of extracellular vesicle (EV)- derived circular RNAs (circRNAs) as diagnostic biomarkers and functional regulators, particularly in vascular remodeling, remain largely undefined. Through circRNA profiling of clinical plasma-derived EVs, this study revealed that EV-circ6853 was elevated in GC plasma and peaked at advanced stages. Its expression level is correlated with poor prognosis, tumor size, and TNM stage. Detection using ddPCR demonstrated superior analytical sensitivity (limit of detection: 4.79 copies/µL). Functionally, EV‑circ6853 was found to play a dual role in regulating the GC vasculature. It functions as a sponge for miR‑627‑5p, activating the FLVCR1/Notch/HIF1A/VEGFA axis to promote angiogenesis while disrupting endothelial cell junctions. Concurrently, it stabilizes HIF1A mRNA by binding to the FUS protein, further enhancing VEGFA‑driven vascular activation. Therapeutically, we constructed a functionalized EV nanoplatform modified with iRGD via genetic engineering and efficiently loaded it with circ6853 siRNA using electroporation. This system achieved active tumor targeting and potent tumor suppression, with favorable biosafety. Our preclinical findings suggest that EV-circ6853 represents a promising preliminary candidate liquid biopsy biomarker and mediates vascular remodeling in gastric cancer. The engineered EV delivery platform provides a novel proof‑of‑concept intervention strategy for RNA-based targeted therapy of GC.

title: NIR light-mediated tumor ferroptosis therapy: a new perspective for multi-modal synergistic therapy
abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, has emerged as a promising strategy for cancer treatment because of its distinct mechanism and potential to overcome conventional drug resistance. However, its clinical application remains limited by insufficient tumor targeting, pronounced heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment, and limited adaptability to individualized treatment. Near-infrared (NIR) imaging provides deep tissue penetration and a low autofluorescence background, offering a feasible approach to spatiotemporally controlled ferroptosis induction and real-time therapeutic monitoring. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in NIR imaging-guided ferroptosis-based therapies and organizes current strategies according to a hierarchical progression from single-modality therapy to dual- and multimodal combinations. We discuss the distinct synergistic mechanisms and design principles at each level and identify major barriers to clinical translation. This framework may provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate combination modalities, designing multifunctional platforms with compatible mechanisms, and developing individualized therapeutic strategies. Finally, we highlight current challenges and future directions for the clinical translation of ferroptosis-targeted theranostics.

title: Hypoxia-preconditioned hair follicle mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes alleviate metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease by facilitating mitophagy through the inhibition of the MEK/ERK signaling pathway
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), characterized by its intricate pathogenesis, is strongly linked to metabolic disorders but currently lacks effective therapeutic strategies. Hair follicle mesenchymal stem cell (HF-MSC)-derived exosomes (Exos) have shown significant efficacy in treating multiple diseases, with hypoxia-preconditioned Exos (Hy-Exos) exerting stronger effects. However, the therapeutic potential of Hy-Exos in MASLD remains unclear. Experimental MASLD models were established through free fatty acid (FFA) stimulation of AML12 cells and high-fat diet treatment in mice. The therapeutic effects of Exos and Hy-Exos were evaluated in cellular and mouse models, and miRNA sequencing was conducted to identify the differences between them. Bioinformatics analysis was used to identify the target genes and related pathways of the miRNAs, which were subsequently verified. Mitochondrial dynamics, mitochondrial function and mitophagy were analyzed through integrated immunofluorescence staining and western blotting. Compared with Exos, Hy-Exos demonstrated an improved efficacy in both the FFA-induced AML12 cells and the high-fat diet-induced MASLD mice. Mechanistically, Hy-Exos exerted their therapeutic effects by inhibiting CDH11 through miR-205-5p to suppress the MEK/ERK signaling pathway, which in turn maintained mitochondrial dynamic stability, restored mitochondrial function and enhanced mitophagy. This study revealed that Hy-Exos inhibited MASLD progression and that CDH11, the target gene of miR-205-5p, may be a major target through which Hy-Exos alleviate MASLD.

title: Spatiotemporally programmed probiotic vaccines potentiate the efficacy of single-epitope neoantigen immunotherapy for solid tumors
abstract: Neoantigen vaccines represent a highly promising strategy for precision cancer immunotherapy due to their tumor specificity and personalized nature. However, single neoantigens peptide often suffer from limited immunogenicity, which restricts their ability to induce robust and durable T cell responses and thus hampers clinical application. Here, we developed a multilayered synergistic platform focusing on single neoantigens peptides by integrating nano‐delivery, in situ immune modulation, and controlled release. The DSPE-PEG-peptide nanovaccine was engineered to actively target tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs), enhancing dendritic cells (DCs) uptake and cross-presentation and consequently strengthening antigen-specific T cell activation and memory formation. In parallel, an engineered probiotics vaccine was generated by covalently coupling an OX40 agonist (αOX40) and the TLR7/8 agonist R848 onto the probiotics, enabling local remodeling of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, amplification of innate signaling, and promotion of DC maturation and T cell infiltration. Both vaccine components were subsequently co-encapsulated within a thermosensitive Poloxamer 407 hydrogel, providing spatial retention and sustained release to maintain continuous immune stimulation. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that this composite system, while preserving the antigenic specificity of single peptides, markedly enhanced DC maturation, strengthened CD8⁺ memory T cell responses, reprogrammed the tumor immune microenvironment, and elicited potent antitumor effects with favorable safety across multiple tumor models. Our findings provide key mechanistic insights and a versatile strategy to enhance the potency of single neoantigen vaccines, paving the way for their clinical translation in personalized cancer immunotherapy.

title: Multi-omics guided self-assembled nanoparticles co-delivering dalbavancin and shTnf-α for synergistic anti-infection and immunomodulation in osteomyelitis
abstract: The treatment of Osteomyelitis (OM) faces challenges due to the harmful cycle of bacterial persistence and pathogen-triggered cytokine storms. Conventional antibiotic therapy centers on eliminating bacteria, yet frequently neglects the immunopathological harm following bacterial breakdown. Therefore, there exists an immediate requirement for dual-action treatments capable of simultaneously alleviating multidrug-resistant infections and hyper-inflammatory reactions. In this study, single-cell sequencing highlights a TNF/NF-κB-centered transcriptional network which serves as a crucial molecular switch, propelling M1 polarization in macrophages related to OM. Combination of network toxicology and transcriptomic investigations uncovers the key regulatory function of TNF in LTA-triggered cytokine storms in OM. Metabolic sequencing reveals that LTA triggers reprogramming of pyrimidine metabolism in macrophages and synergistically boosts Tnf-α expression. As a result, we created DB-shTnf-α@Gel, an injectable hydrogel that delivers Dalbavancin and shTnf-α self-assembled nanoparticles. This system demonstrated strong anti- MRSA efficacy and interfered with bacterial resistance genes in vitro. In vivo experiments revealed that DB-shTnf-α@Gel has the capacity to oppose macrophage M1 polarization and notably relieve bone damage. By accurately zeroing in on TNF-induced excessive inflammation and eliminating multidrug-resistant infections, this nanoplatform presents a synergistic, phased therapeutic approach to surmount the intricate pathology of OM.

title: Lipid nanoparticle-mediated delivery of bta-miR-149-5p and bta-miR-1307 alleviates Mycoplasma bovis-induced mastitis via targeted regulation of macrophage inflammatory responses
abstract: Mycoplasma bovis ( M. bovis ) is a major causative agent of bovine mastitis, and increasing antibiotic resistance highlights the urgent need for alternative therapeutic strategies. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) serve as key mediators of host-pathogen communication by transferring regulatory microRNAs (miRNAs). In this study, we aimed to elucidate the functional roles of EV-associated miRNAs in M. bovis -induced inflammation and explore the therapeutic potential of lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mediated miRNA delivery. We found that M. bovis infection remodeled the miRNA profile of EVs derived from bovine mammary epithelial cells (MAC-T), with a marked reduction in the abundance of bta-miR-149-5p and bta-miR-1307. Both bta-miR-149-5p and bta-miR-1307 were verified to negatively regulate M. bovis -induced inflammatory responses in BoMac cells. Mechanistically, bta-miR-149-5p directly targeted MAPK14 and suppressed the p38-MAPK/ATF2 signaling pathway, while bta-miR-1307 targeted MAP2K3 to inhibit M. bovis -induced inflammatory responses. Furthermore, co-overexpression of two miRNAs attenuated M. bovis -induced macrophage inflammatory responses, suggesting their potential combined regulatory effects. Additionally, we established a murine mastitis model and found Cy3-labeled, RGD-conjugated LNPs efficiently delivered bta-miR-149-5p and bta-miR-1307 mimics into mammary gland tissues. LNP-mediated co-delivery alleviated M. bovis -induced mastitis, as evidenced by reduced histopathological damage, decreased Ly6G-positive neutrophil infiltration, and reduced expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Collectively, this study reveals a novel EV-mediated miRNA regulatory axis utilized by M. bovis to facilitate macrophage inflammatory responses, wherein bta-miR-149-5p and bta-miR-1307 serve as critical anti-inflammatory modulators. LNP-mediated co-delivery of these miRNAs further offers a potential non-antibiotic therapeutic strategy to alleviate M. bovis -induced mastitis.

title: Biomimetic metal-phenolic networks targeting crystal-associated macrophages for PANoptosis attenuation and microenvironment remodeling of calcium oxalate kidney stone
abstract: Persistent chronic inflammation driven by calcium oxalate (CaOx) crystals contributes to the occurrence and recurrence of kidney stone, in which macrophages play a central role in crystal clearance and inflammatory regulation. Here, we developed a biomimetic metal–phenolic network (4OI@CAM-MPNs) designed to target crystal-associated macrophages and modulate their inflammatory state. The platform comprises a manganese–luteolin (Mn-Lu) coordination network as the core to load anti-inflammatory metabolite 4-octyl itaconate (4OI), cloaked with a renal tubular epithelial–macrophage hybrid membrane modified with osteopontin (OPN) peptides and D-mannose. The dual-targeting design enables macrophage recognition through D-mannose–CD206 interactions and CaOx crystal association through OPN–crystal interactions, thereby facilitating preferential localization to crystal-associated macrophages. Results show 4OI@CAM-MPNs possess favorable in vivo targeting and multi-enzyme mimetic activity, enabling clearance of excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the pathological microenvironment. Mechanistically, 4OI@CAM-MPNs activate Nrf2 and suppress the IFN-β/ZBP1 signaling axis, thereby suppressing macrophage PANoptosis induced by crystal overloading and restoring their phagocytic clearance function. Single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed that 4OI@CAM-MPNs remodeled macrophage functional states by reducing inflammatory populations while promoting reparative phenotypes. Moreover, inhibition of SPP1-mediated pathological crosstalk alleviated stromal–immune dysregulation, renal tubular injury, and fibrosis. Overall, this study provides a feasible nanotherapeutic strategy for CaOx stone via targeting crystal-associated macrophages, regulating macrophage PANoptosis, and restoring renal immune homeostasis.

title: Engineered adipose stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles lead to significant improvement of motor function after ischemic stroke by ameliorating neuroinflammation via miR-221-3p delivery
abstract: Adipose stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (ADSC-EVs) have recently emerged as a promising therapeutic agent for mitigating inflammation following ischemic stroke (IS). However, elucidating precisely how ADSC-EVs exert their effects and engineering functionally enhanced, well-targeted ADSC-EVs remain significant challenges. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential of intranasally delivered ADSC-EVs in IS mice, elucidate the underlying mechanism by which ADSC-EVs suppress microglial and inflammatory responses through miR-221-3p delivery, and develop functionally enhanced EVs engineered with this key therapeutic miRNA (miR-221-3p). To evaluate the therapeutic effects and biosafety, we performed behavioral tests, histological and immunofluorescence staining, and initial safety assessments. For mechanistic investigation, we utilized RNA sequencing, Western blot, and a rescue experiment with a constitutively active IKKβ mutant (IKKβ-CA) to confirm pathway specificity. Engineered EVs overexpressing miR-221-3p were constructed for functional validation. We found that ADSC-EVs efficiently reached the ischemic brain and were internalized by microglia, with higher uptake in the pro-inflammatory M1 state. Treatment significantly reduced infarct volume and improved neurological and motor function. Mechanistic investigations using primary microglia and a microglia-neuron co-culture system revealed that ADSC-EVs inhibited microglial inflammation and neuronal apoptosis, thereby creating a more protective microenvironment. We identified miR-221-3p as a key mediator enriched within ADSC-EVs. This miRNA mediated the observed effects by targeting the IKKβ/NF-κB signaling pathway in microglia, confirmed by rescue experiments with a constitutively active IKKβ mutant. Functional validation using engineered ADSC-EVs overexpressing miR-221-3p confirmed the enhanced efficacy in suppressing M1 polarization and amplifying neuroprotection. Notably, engineered ADSC-EVs conferred protection even at lower doses, and initial safety assessments revealed no toxicity or chronic inflammation. We demonstrated that miR-221-3p delivered by ADSC-EVs suppressed microglial M1 polarization via the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway. This suppression inhibited neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis, leading to motor functional recovery after ischemic stroke. Repeated intranasal administration of engineered ADSC-EVs showed no detectable toxicity, chronic inflammation, or tumorigenicity, and the therapeutic benefits on motor function were sustained over time. This study elucidates a detailed mechanistic pathway and proposes a novel, safe, and effective therapeutic strategy using miRNA-enriched engineered EVs for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

title: A Multifunctional Nb2C MXene-based hydrogel supports mesenchymal stem cell therapy for subacute spinal cord injury
abstract: Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy is a promising strategy for spinal cord injury (SCI), but its efficacy is limited by poor cell retention and impaired function within the inflammatory and oxidative lesion microenvironment. Here, we developed an injectable and tissue-adhesive HAFN hydrogel incorporating PDA-modified Nb₂C MXene nanosheets as a local platform for MSC delivery after SCI. HAFN exhibited favorable injectability, tissue adhesion, electrical conductivity, and reactive oxygen species-scavenging activity. In vitro, HAFN protected MSCs against oxidative stress, while HAFN-supported MSC treatment attenuated macrophage inflammatory responses and improved neural cell survival and migration. HAFN also supported neural-associated differentiation of MSCs in vitro. In a rat SCI model, treatment was administered at 7 days after injury to represent a subacute intervention. MSC-encapsulated HAFN improved local MSC retention and reduced oxidative stress, inflammation, and neuronal apoptosis. These effects were accompanied by reduced astroglial accumulation and improved neural tissue preservation, axonal and synaptic remodeling, and myelin repair, ultimately leading to better locomotor recovery. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed coordinated changes in inflammatory and cell-survival programs. Collectively, these findings identify HAFN as a multifunctional platform that integrates MSC delivery, redox regulation, immune modulation, and neural tissue repair, thereby improving the retention and therapeutic performance of MSCs for subacute SCI treatment.

title: Barrier to bypass: a PEI-functionalized star polycation platform for potent broad-spectrum aphid RNAi management
abstract: Star polycation (SPc) has been validated as an efficient RNA delivery carrier, yet its limited RNA-binding capacity, formulation stability and multi-barrier penetration restrict its cost-effective application in sprayable RNA pesticides. Here, we functionalized SPc with polyethyleneimine (PEI) to develop a series of SPcP nanoparticles, rationally integrating SPc’s protective capacity with PEI’s cationic charges and membrane-interactive features. Among synthesized SPcP nanoparticles, SPcP3 formed compact spherical nanocomplexes with dsRNA through electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding and Van der Waals forces. Notably, SPcP3 complexation not only markedly enhanced RNA stability against nuclease, thermal and extreme pH challenges, but also significantly improved leaf surface deposition, aphid cuticle penetration and cellular internalization. Transcriptomic profiling in Sf9 cells revealed that the SPcP3-mediated delivery enhancement arose from coordinated activation of endocytosis, vesicle trafficking, lysosome-related processes and transmembrane transport, which was consistent with the proposed “proton sponge” effect and identified a previously unrecognized auxiliary transport route. Leveraging this platform, we screened conserved sequences of ATP-d , CHS and EcR across five aphid species and assembled them into a multi-target shRNA formulation (shRNAs/SPcP3). This formulation achieved stable broad-spectrum control against five aphid species, with laboratory control efficacies of 87.3%–96.9%, while exhibiting excellent biocompatibility-no obvious adverse impacts on cucumber growth, natural enemy Harmonia axyridis or Sf9 cells. Collectively, this study establishes a robust nano-platform that overcomes the major delivery barriers limiting RNA pesticide application, offering a scalable and eco-friendly strategy for broad-spectrum aphid management.

title: Emerging roles of stem cells and exosomes in male reproductive injury: mechanisms, engineering approaches, and therapeutic potential
abstract: Male reproductive injuries—including erectile dysfunction (ED), chemotherapy/radiotherapy-induced testicular damage, epididymal dysfunction, and oligoasthenoteratozoospermia—represent a growing global health burden. Current therapies offer limited efficacy for refractory cases. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and their small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) have emerged as promising regenerative strategies capable of repairing reproductive microenvironments through cell replacement, paracrine modulation, and immunoregulation. This review highlights sEVs, commonly referred to as exosomes in the literature, as natural nanocarriers and discusses advanced nanoengineering strategies for precision delivery. This review systematically examines therapeutic mechanisms across three organs with markedly different levels of translational maturity: (i) in the corpus cavernosum, where the most advanced evidence exists, including early-phase clinical trials, EV-associated miRNAs (miR-126-3p, miR-210-3p) and lncRNAs (MALAT1) modulate inflammation, angiogenesis, and fibrosis; (ii) in the testis, where evidence remains predominantly preclinical with limited early human data, miR-34c-3p/GDNF signaling promotes spermatogonial stem cell self-renewal, while mitochondrial transfer restores Leydig cell testosterone synthesis; and (iii) in the epididymis, a substantially more exploratory area where direct in vivo studies are scarce and most evidence is derived from in vitro or indirect observations, region-specific cargoes (USP44/RBM14, miR-199a-3p/VHL/HIF-1α, circRNAs) maintain sperm maturation and epigenetic reprogramming. Nanotechnology platforms may enhance therapeutic precision: PLGA nanoparticles prolong circulation, GelMA hydrogels enable sustained release, and magnetic soft microrobots provide enhanced targeting efficiency. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate that MSC/exosome-based therapy significantly improves erectile function, reduces germ cell apoptosis, and increases sperm maturation. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate that MSC/exosome-based therapies improve functional recovery through paracrine mechanisms, anti-inflammatory effects, and promotion of angiogenesis, with improvements in erectile function, reduced germ cell apoptosis, and increased sperm maturation in animal models. However, clinical evidence remains limited. A small number of early-phase trials have reported preliminary safety findings and potential efficacy signals in PDE5i-nonresponsive ED and non-obstructive azoospermia; these findings are insufficient to establish validated safety or efficacy, and larger controlled trials are needed. Critical challenges remain: lack of standardized GMP protocols (inter-batch CV > 15%), incomplete long-term safety and biodistribution data, and no FDA/EMA approval for any regenerative therapy in this field as of 2026. Future directions include multi-omics (scRNA-seq, spatial omics), organoid platforms, synthetic sEVs, and AI-guided precision therapy based on genetic profiles (e.g., CYP19A1 rs10046). By integrating stem cell biology, exosome science, and nanotechnology, this review aims to provide a framework for developing next-generation precision nanomedicines for male reproductive health.

title: Engineering the bandgap of TiO2 nanorods through copper doping: a dual-modal strategy for radiosensitization and cuproptosis activation
abstract: Although titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) semiconductor nanomaterials have garnered considerable attention in radiotherapy research due to their photoelectric effect, the inefficient electron-hole (e – -h + ) separation limits reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation upon X-ray irradiation in the tumor microenvironment (TME), restricting the therapeutic effect. Herein, we doped TiO 2 nanorods with various transition metals (Mn, Fe, Co, and Cu) to tailor their bandgap structures. Among these, Cu-doped TiO 2 nanorods (Cu-TiO 2 NRs) demonstrated the most outstanding performance during radiotherapy. On one hand, the incorporation of Cu in TiO 2 narrows the bandgap, enhances e⁻-h⁺ separation, and promotes ROS generation under irradiation. Meanwhile, Cu 2+ on the surface can act as traps to capture photoelectrons, converting into Cu + with Fenton-like reactivity, boosting ROS level in the TME. What’s more, the accumulated Cu + effectively induced cuproptosis in tumor cells, thereby overcoming tumor radioresistance and enhancing the therapeutic effect. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that Cu-TiO 2 NRs combined with low-dose X-ray irradiation significantly inhibited tumor growth. These findings establish copper-doping engineering as a promising strategy for achieving synergistic cancer therapy by integrating radiotherapy with cuproptosis induction, offering a safe and effective approach for clinical translation.

title: Nanoparticle-based T-cell engagers: from T-cell redirection to programmable immune platforms
abstract: Bispecific T-cell engagers (BTCEs) have emerged as a powerful class of cancer immunotherapies that redirect endogenous T cells toward malignant cells through the simultaneous binding of T cells and cancer cells via tumor-associated antigens (TAAs). Despite remarkable clinical success, particularly in hematologic malignancies, conventional BTCEs face significant limitations, including short circulation half-lives, rapid renal clearance, antigen-loss-mediated resistance, and reduced efficacy in solid tumors due to the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Nanoparticle-based bispecific T-cell engagers (nanoBTCEs) have been developed to address these challenges by combining the immune-engaging capabilities of BTCEs with the pharmacokinetic and engineering advantages of nanomedicine. In this review, we discuss how nanotechnology expands the therapeutic capabilities of T-cell engagers beyond simple immune redirection. NanoBTCEs enhance T-cell recruitment and tumor engagement through multivalent interactions, improve pharmacokinetic properties, and enable multifunctional therapeutic strategies through the incorporation of immunomodulatory payloads, therapeutic cargos, and imaging agents. Emerging platforms have demonstrated the ability to modulate the TME, reverse T-cell dysfunction and exhaustion, integrate theranostic functionalities, and overcome tumor heterogeneity and antigen escape through multispecific targeting approaches. Altogether, these advances position nanoBTCEs as versatile immunotherapeutic platforms rather than simple T-cell-engaging agents. We further discuss key translational challenges, outstanding biological questions, and future design principles for next generation nanoBTCEs. As the fields of nanotechnology and immunoengineering continue to converge, nanoBTCEs are evolving into programmable immune platforms capable of integrating T-cell redirection, precision delivery, TME modulation, and multimodal therapeutic functions within a single construct. Collectively, these advances highlight the potential of nanoBTCEs to overcome several limitations of conventional BTCEs and broaden the clinical utility of T-cell-based cancer immunotherapies.

title: A trivalent mRNA vaccine elicits robust immune responses and confers potent protection against heterologous CCHFV challenge in mice
abstract: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF) is a life-threatening hemorrhagic fever caused by Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), with a broad geographic distribution and a high case fatality rate up to 70%. However, there are no licensed vaccines or therapeutic drugs against CCHF. Here, we developed CC-GGN24, a trivalent mRNA vaccine encoding three antigenic components (MLD-GP38, Gc, and NP) from the CCHFV IbAr10200 strain. Two doses of CC-GGN24 elicited robust humoral and cellular immune responses in mice. Monovalent mRNA vaccines encoding MLD-GP38, Gc, or GPC confer partial protection against heterologous CCHFV YL16070 challenge, whereas CC-GGN24 and NP monovalent mRNA vaccines provide complete protection in IFNAR -/- mice. Notably, CC-GGN24 outperformed the NP monovalent mRNA vaccines in the efficiency of viral clearance and mitigates pathological damage. Even an ultra-low dose of 0.2 µg of CC-GGN24 was sufficient to protect against lethal homologous and heterologous viral challenges. Overall, our findings demonstrate that the trivalent mRNA vaccine conferred potent and broad protection against CCHFV, and provides valuable insights for future broad-spectrum vaccine development against viral hemorrhagic fevers.

title: A hyaluronidase-responsive nano in micro depot improves chondrocyte-level teriparatide delivery for osteoarthritis treatment
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disease with a growing clinical burden. Current treatments mainly provide symptomatic relief and have limited ability to slow structural progression. Teriparatide (TP), a clinically approved parathyroid hormone analogue, has shown potential for protecting chondrocytes and supporting cartilage matrix homeostasis. However, its application in OA remains limited by poor intra-articular availability, including rapid joint clearance, limited access to cartilage, and insufficient exposure at the chondrocyte level. To address these barriers, we developed a nano-in-micro sequential intra-articular delivery system, TP@P-Lipo@HM. In this system, TP was loaded into FGL-modified cationic liposomes (~ 100 nm), which were then encapsulated within methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA) microspheres (~ 150 μm). Rather than requiring a single carrier to simultaneously achieve prolonged joint retention and efficient cartilage transport, the two structural scales were assigned complementary functions: the microscale HAMA compartment served as a retained intra-articular depot and enabled hyaluronidase-responsive liberation of the nanoscale liposomes, whereas the released P-Lipo promoted cartilage-associated distribution and enhanced uptake by OA chondrocytes. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that TP@P-Lipo@HM improved chondrocyte anabolic–catabolic homeostasis, reduced inflammation and apoptosis, preserved cartilage structure, and attenuated OA progression. Thus, this nano-in-micro architecture provides a sequential strategy that decouples joint retention from tissue/cellular delivery and offers a practical platform for improving the local delivery of TP in OA.

title: 3D bioprinting of tissue-engineered bladder patches containing neurovascular networks using conductive microgel
abstract: Current tissue-engineered bladder patches are hindered by the absence of coordinated neurovascular regeneration, which limits their functional repair capacity. This study aimed to develop a neurovascularized bladder patch (NVBP) and assess its efficacy in bladder defect repair. GelMA-MXene (GM) conductive hydrogel microspheres encapsulating adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) were initially prepared to induce efficient differentiation of ADSCs into neural and vascular lineages within a conductive microenvironment. These pre-differentiated neural and vascular microspheres were then formulated into a microgel bioink, facilitating the construction of the NVBP using 3D bioprinting technology. Results indicated that GM microspheres enhanced ADSCs viability, proliferation, and stemness markers (Sox2/Nanog). Upon induction, GM microspheres upregulated the expression of neural-related genes (TUBB3, MAP2, Nestin, GAP43) and vascular-related genes (KDR, ANGPT1). Transcriptomic analysis and validation results demonstrated that the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway was significantly enriched, and the expression of Tnn and Pik3cd genes within it was also upregulated. This pathway might contribute to the effect on MXene’s promotion of ADSCs’ differentiation into neural and vascular lineages. The microgel bioink exhibited shear-thinning behavior, a broad printing temperature range, and excellent self-healing and fatigue resistance. The 3D bioprinted NVBP effectively maintained stable neural and vascular phenotypes. In an in vivo rat model, NVBP significantly enhanced bladder capacity (923.76 ± 119.80 µL) and compliance (27.04 ± 5.22 µL/mmHg). Histological analysis revealed improved smooth muscle organization, reduced collagen deposition, and significantly increased areas positive for βIII-Tubulin, PECAM1, and α-SMA in the NVBP group. In summary, NVBP promotes rat bladder tissue remodeling and functional recovery through synergistic neurovascular regeneration, offering a novel biomimetic strategy for bladder tissue engineering and is worthy of further in-depth research. 3D bioprinting of tissue-engineered bladder patches containing neurovascular networks using conductive microgel

title: Erianin-loaded biomimetic nanoadjuvant alleviates exhaustion-like CD8⁺ T-cell dysfunction and enhances radiotherapy-induced antitumor immunity
abstract: CD8⁺ T-cell exhaustion limits the efficacy of immunotherapy in solid tumors, and strategies that preserve T-cell metabolic fitness remain insufficient. Here, we found that erianin, a natural small molecule, alleviates exhaustion-like dysfunction and improves effector function in CD8 + T cells under persistent stimulatory stress, although its poor aqueous solubility and limited bioavailability restrict its therapeutic application. To improve the delivery of erianin and integrate immune-stimulatory function, we developed a biomimetic composite nanoadjuvant (PPEC), composed of a PC7A-based Polyplex core co-loaded with erianin and Poly(I: C) and coated with tumor-cell-membrane vesicles. In vitro, PPEC promoted BMDC uptake and maturation, and cytokine production consistent with an activated antigen-presenting phenotype, and preserved CD8⁺ T-cell effector activity. Comparative formulation studies further showed that the anti-exhaustion activity of the system was mainly derived from erianin. Mechanistically, erianin-associated recovery of mitochondrial function was accompanied by RXRα- associated changes in the ITPR2/MCU calcium-handling pathway and reduced mitochondria-associated Ca²⁺ accumulation. In poorly immunogenic Lewis lung carcinoma models, local administration of PPEC suppressed tumor growth, enhanced the therapeutic efficacy of radiotherapy, increased dendritic-cell maturation and CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and reduced selected features of intratumoral T-cell dysfunction. This work presents a mechanism-guided nanoadjuvant strategy that combines dendritic-cell activation with metabolic protection of T cells for solid tumor immunotherapy.

title: Deep-learning-predicted sinomenine ameliorates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease by delaying cellular senescence via NES
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common metabolic liver disorder worldwide, and its burden is growing as populations age and obesity rates rise. Current therapies only partially correct metabolic disturbances and fail to reverse hepatocyte senescence or restore functional capacity. Here, we built a deep-learning efficacy prediction system (DLEPS) powered by L1000 transcriptomic data to screen bioactive compounds and identified the natural alkaloid sinomenine (Sino) as a potent MASLD modulator. Mechanistically, Sino suppresses the transcriptional activity of NF-κB and thereby downregulates NES expression. NES emerged as an important intermediate mediator linking NF-κB signaling to hepatocyte senescence. Reduced NES expression was associated with lower Smad3 phosphorylation and reduced P53/P21 pathway activation, delays cellular senescence, inhibits the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), and restores normal mitochondrial structure and metabolic function. To enhance hepatic delivery, we further engineered galactose-lipid-membrane-coated Sino nanoparticles (Gal-SiNPs), which enhanced hepatic accumulation and retained therapeutic activity at a relatively lower administered dose. Collectively, deep-learning-guided discovery of Sino reshapes hepatocyte function via the NES -senescence pathway, and its nano-targeted formulation shows promising therapeutic potential for MASLD therapy and merits further translational exploration.

title: Glycan-targeted gold nanorod nanoplatform for photothermal immunotherapy of pancreatic cancer
abstract: Despite the clinical successes of adaptive immune checkpoint blockade, sialic acid-mediated interactions associated with the Siglec-10/CD24 “don’t eat me” pathway can contribute to impaired macrophage-mediated clearance in pancreatic cancer. Here, we report a dual-targeting gold nanorod platform (Man-AuNR-SNA) designed to combine glycan-mediated targeting with photothermal therapy. The nanoplatform targets CD206-expressing M2-like macrophages via mannose and recognizes sialylated pancreatic cancer cells via SNA lectin. Dual functionalization enhanced macrophage–cancer cell interactions compared with single-target controls, supporting complementary contributions of mannose- and SNA-mediated targeting. NIR-triggered photothermal treatment induced apoptotic cancer cell death and, in a PANC-1 xenograft model, achieved 70.9% tumor growth inhibition, comparable to that observed with gemcitabine. Treatment was also associated with an increased CD86/CD206 ratio and changes in macrophage-associated gene expression consistent with a more pro-inflammatory phenotype. These findings support the integration of glycan-mediated macrophage–cancer cell targeting with photothermal therapy as a potential strategy for pancreatic cancer treatment.

title: Chylomicron-biomimetic nanoparticles enable efficient intestinal lymphatic transport for oral delivery of therapeutic proteins
abstract: Abstract Intestinal lymphatic transport (ILT) represents a promising pathway for the oral absorption of macromolecular drugs, but the formation of lipid droplet is a rate-limiting step during ILT. In this study, we developed a chylomicron (CM)-biomimetic nanoparticle constructed from CM components, characterized by high lipoprotein affinity, to enable efficient oral delivery of the anti-fibrotic protein klotho via ILT. This approach demonstrated potent therapeutic efficacy in the treatment of renal fibrosis. The nanoparticle exhibited size stability and retained 78.3% enzyme activity after 12 hours of incubation in simulated digestive fluid, while facilitating rapid diffusion through the mucus layer. Within enterocytes, the nanoparticle underwent a CM-like transcytosis process and showed a preference for ILT, as evidenced by cannulation into the main mesenteric lymphatic duct in rats. Notably, this biocompatible oral nanoparticle achieved an absolute bioavailability of 2.7%, delivering superior anti-fibrotic activity in a mouse disease model compared to a 125-fold higher dose of intraperitoneally administered captopril, a first-line anti-fibrotic drug. Our innovative nanoparticle design based on high lipoprotein affinity enables enhanced oral absorption of macromolecular drugs via ILT.

title: Spatiotemporally programmed biomimetic liposome coordinates vascular and immune modulation in pulmonary arterial hypertension
abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains a progressive and fatal vascular disease despite substantial advances in vasodilator-based therapies. Combining anti-inflammatory intervention with established vasodilator treatment represents a promising disease-modifying strategy for PAH. Here, persistent IL-6-associated inflammatory remodeling has been identified as an important driver of pulmonary vascular remodeling that persists despite standard vasodilator therapy. Guided by this insight, a biomimetic, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanoplatform, Lipo@MM-Maci-Pep@TCZ, was developed for the coordinated delivery of the vasodilator macitentan and the anti-IL-6 receptor antibody tocilizumab to diseased pulmonary vasculature. This programmable core–shell nanoplatform integrates a macitentan-loaded diselenide liposomal core for ROS-triggered drug release, macrophage membrane cloaking for inflammation-guided vascular targeting and endothelial interaction, and an RGD-containing self-assembling peptide interface for tocilizumab loading, thereby enabling enhanced antibody encapsulation and prolonged pulmonary retention. Lipo@MM-Maci-Pep@TCZ executes a sequential delivery cascade involving adhesion to inflamed endothelium, transendothelial transport, lesion-specific disassembly, and synchronized drug release within the immune-vascular microenvironment. In two independent experimental PAH models, this dual-drug nanotherapy reduced right ventricular systolic pressure, right ventricular hypertrophy, pulmonary vascular remodeling, fibrosis, macrophage infiltration, and smooth muscle cell proliferation, outperforming monotherapy and free-drug combinations. Transcriptomic analysis revealed the coordinated suppression of inflammatory signaling and of pathogenic smooth muscle cell remodeling programs, the reprogramming of macrophage-associated inflammatory pathways, and the restoration of endothelial homeostasis through simultaneous inhibition of endothelin- and IL-6-driven signaling. Collectively, these results demonstrate a microenvironment-responsive combinatorial nanomedicine strategy that integrates vasodilatory and immune-targeted therapy, establishing a promising therapeutic framework for PAH and potentially other inflammatory vascular diseases.

title: Biodegradable polymer-enabled ROS-responsive nanogels for controlled drug release and boosted cancer treatment
abstract: Biodegradable nanogels (NGs) have emerged as promising platforms for controlled drug delivery free of long-term biosafety concerns. Reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanomaterials have garnered increasing attention as smart drug delivery systems exploiting the aberrant redox environment of tumors for precise and efficient therapy. We developed biodegradable, biocompatible, and crosslinkable polymer-based ROS-responsive NGs to enable controlled drug release and enhanced cancer treatment outcomes. Three different ROS-responsive drug linkers, featuring thioether and ester groups separated by varied lengths of carbon chains, were exploited to attach paclitaxel (PTX) molecules to the NG scaffold. The PTX-NGs were fabricated through a mild polymer-crosslinking process, yielding spherical nanoparticles with an average diameter of ~60 nm, which facilitated cellular internalization and tumor penetration. Leveraging the elevated intracellular ROS levels of cancer cells to trigger the release of PTX, PTX-NGs exhibited efficient tumor inhibition while minimizing systemic toxicities. Notably, the anticancer therapeutic efficiencies of different NGs were determined by the ROS-responsive drug linkers, specifically the length of carbon chains between the thioether and ester groups. In addition, the PTX-NGs were well tolerated by mice during long-term administration, exhibiting desired biocompatibility. Overall, this work highlights the advantages of biodegradable ROS-responsive polymeric NGs serving as an advanced drug delivery platform for boosted cancer treatment.

title: Catechol-based antioxidant nanoplatform alleviates chondrocyte senescence and osteoarthritis via ATM/ATR-PINK1-mediated mitophagy
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease associated with cellular senescence and mitochondrial dysfunction. Although epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) and D-methionine (D-Met) exhibit antioxidant and anti-senescent activities, poor bioavailability and rapid intra-articular clearance limit their therapeutic potential. Here, we developed an EGCG-based antioxidant nanoparticle, ED@F127 nanoparticles (NPs), by conjugating EGCG with D-Met through a green Mannich reaction, followed by encapsulation in Pluronic F127. The resulting NPs exhibited a uniform size of approximately 80 nm, high drug-loading efficiency, and favorable biocompatibility. Using basic calcium phosphate (BCP) crystals as an OA-relevant pathological stimulus, we showed that ED@F127 NPs attenuated BCP-induced chondrocyte senescence. ED@F127 NPs also increased ATM/ATR abundance and PINK1/PARKIN-associated mitophagy markers. These changes were accompanied by reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation and improved mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP-associated signals. In vivo , intra-articular administration of ED@F127 NPs alleviated cartilage degeneration, abnormal subchondral bone remodeling, and osteophyte formation in a BCP crystal-induced rat OA model. Together, these findings support ED@F127 NPs as a promising nanotherapeutic strategy for attenuating oxidative stress and cellular senescence in OA.

title: Injectable and reactive oxygen species-responsive nanogel–microgel hybrid bio-lubricants for osteoarthritis therapy by immunometabolic reprogramming
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disorder involving irreversible cartilage damage, subchondral bone dysfunction, and chronic synovitis. Current intra-articular therapies suffer from short-lived effects and inadequate control of macrophage-mediated inflammation. To address this limitation, we develop an injectable, ROS-responsive nanogel–microgel hybrid bio-lubricant for OA treatment via immunometabolic reprogramming. Skatole-loaded mesoporous silica nanoparticles were crosslinked with polyvinyl alcohol to form ROS-responsive nanogels (Ska@NGs), which were subsequently encapsulated into HAMA/CSMA microgels using microfluidics as Ska@N-MGs. The physicochemical, rheological, lubricating, ROS-responsive, and biological properties of the system were evaluated in vitro, followed by therapeutic assessment in an ACLT + MMT-induced rat OA model. Ska@N-MGs exhibited favorable lubricating and ROS-regulating properties, with a friction coefficient of approximately 0.007. Skatole attenuated inflammatory responses in LPS-stimulated macrophages, while Ska@NGs treatment in the macrophage–chondrocyte co-culture system was accompanied by improved cartilage matrix-related markers. In a rat OA model, intra-articular injection of Ska@N-MGs reduced synovial inflammation and alleviated OA progression. This hybrid system integrates lubrication, stimuli-responsive drug delivery, and immunometabolic modulation, providing a promising platform for OA therapy.

title: Bacterial missile with ultrasound-triggered prodrug release for targeted pancreatic cancer therapy
abstract: Pancreatic cancer poses a severe clinical challenge owing to its deep-seated site, inefficient drug delivery, poor tumor penetration, and systemic toxicity of conventional chemotherapy. Herein, we fabricated an ultrasound-responsive “bacterial missile” via in situ atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) on attenuated Salmonella VNP20009. Thioketal-linked 5-fluorouracil (5-Fu) prodrugs were densely grafted onto bacteria to form a protective polymer shell, enabling high drug loading, reducing off-target toxicity, and shielding surface antigens to alleviate excessive immunogenicity. Manganese carbonate (MnCO 3 ) nanoparticles were further assembled onto the engineered bacteria to construct VNP@P5-Fu@Mn. Under ultrasound irradiation, reactive oxygen species cleave thioketal bonds for on-demand 5-Fu release, while released Mn 2+ activates the cGAS–STING pathway. The living bacterial chassis actively penetrates dense tumor stroma and targets deep lesions. In vitro and in vivo studies confirm that this system induces robust immunogenic cell death, promotes dendritic cell maturation, enhances CD8 + T-cell infiltration, and effectively inhibits orthotopic pancreatic tumor growth with minimal systemic toxicity. This work integrates bacterial targeting, ultrasound-controlled prodrug activation, and cGAS–STING-mediated immunotherapy, offering a programmable and translatable living therapeutic platform for precise treatment of deep-seated solid tumors. We developed an ultrasound-responsive “bacterial missile” by grafting chemotherapy prodrugs onto attenuated Salmonella via ATRP. This system leverages bacterial tumor targeting for deep accumulation and uses ultrasound for precise drug release at the tumor site, enhancing efficacy while minimizing off-target damage to normal tissues. This strategy offers a promising approach for precise deep-tumor therapy.

title: Correction: High-throughput synthesis and optimization of ionizable lipids through A3 coupling for efficient mRNA delivery
pH-responsive HA/chitosan nanoplatform delivering deer antler polypeptide to induce DNA damage and checkpoint imbalance for TNBC therapy
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks effective targeted therapeutic options and often relies on stress-adaptation pathways for survival. Deer antler peptides (DAP) is a complex mixture of peptides and proteins with potential bioactivity, but its therapeutic application is limited by delivery inefficiency. In this study, we characterized DAP, investigated its antitumor effects in TNBC, and developed a pH-responsive hyaluronic acid/chitosan nanodelivery system (CS-HA-DAP) to improve its biological performance. Proteomic analysis identified 79 proteins and 122 peptides in DAP; DAP consisted mainly of low- to medium-molecular-weight proteins and peptides and dose-dependently inhibited the viability of 4T1 cells, with half-maximal inhibitory concentrations of 1.62 mg/mL, and also impaired migration and invasion of 4T1 cells, with relatively lower toxicity toward normal MCF-10 A cells. Transcriptomic and molecular analyses showed that DAP induced persistent DNA damage-associated stress, time-dependent γ-H2AX accumulation, incomplete sustained CHK1 activation, and dysregulation of cell-cycle regulators, together with pyroptosis- and ferroptosis-related changes, which were rescuable by Fer-1 and VX-765. CETSA showed that GDQGPVGR physically bound TOP2A and CHK1, and docking together with inhibitor-combination assays supported the involvement of TOP2A- and CHK1-related processes; furthermore, DAP exhibited synergy with etoposide and MK-8776. To improve delivery, we constructed CS-HA-DAP nanoparticles by coupling DAP to hyaluronic acid via EDC and NHS conjugation followed by ionic gelation with chitosan and tripolyphosphate. The optimized nanoparticles, which showed spherical morphology and measured 158.2 nm with a zeta potential of +28.7 mV, achieved a high encapsulation efficiency of 89.2% and a drug loading capacity of 57.2%. They also showed marked pH-responsive release, with substantially higher cumulative release at pH 5.0 than at pH 7.4, reaching 89.18% at pH 5.0 versus 23.43% at pH 7.4 over 48 h. CS-HA-DAP enhanced the inhibitory effects of free DAP on 4T1 cell viability, migration, and invasion while maintaining relatively low toxicity toward MCF-10 A cells. In orthotopic 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, orally administered CS-HA-DAP showed tumor-associated fluorescence signals in tumors, suppressed tumor growth more effectively than free DAP, achieving a tumor growth inhibition (TGI) rate of 85.74% versus 53.57%, and exhibited acceptable preliminary biosafety. DAP is a bioactive peptide mixture with antitumor activity associated with sustained genomic stress and checkpoint imbalance in TNBC, and CS-HA-DAP represents an effective nanodelivery strategy that enhances its therapeutic efficacy, with improved tumor accumulation and acceptable preliminary safety. This work provides a nanobiotechnology-based approach for improving the antitumor potential of complex natural peptide mixtures and offers a promising lead for further translational development.

title: Core–shell structural calcium-deposited manganese-copper oxide that induces immunogenic cell death and STING activation for augmented metalloimmunotherapy of triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: Metal ions mediated tumor immunotherapy showed considerable potential in clinical application, but the efficacy of single metal ion elicited immune response was relatively low. Herein, we developed a PDGFB cyclopeptide modified core–shell structural calcium-deposited manganese-copper oxide (CMC) for enhanced metalloimmunotherapy of triple-negative breast cancer. Due to the overexpression of PDGFR-β receptors, PCMC selectively recognised 4T1 cells, efficiently entering the tumor cells and triggering the release of substantial amounts of Cu, Mn, and Ca ions. These Cu ions catalysed Fenton-like reactions, rapidly increasing intracellular ROS levels, thereby inducing cuproptosis in tumor cells and promoting calreticulin exposure and HMGB1 release with confirmed ICD. Additionally, Mn ions activated the cGAS-STING signalling pathway, enhancing dendritic cell (DC) maturation, promoting cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) infiltration, and boosting the anti-tumor immune response. Ca ions disrupted intracellular calcium homeostasis, synergistically enhancing ROS production and potentiating cGAS-STING activation, further amplifying the anti-tumor immunotherapy. In vitro and organoid assays confirmed that PCMC-mediated ROS production effectively induced tumor cuproptosis and calreticulin exposure and HMGB1 release. In vivo, PCMC markedly promoted DC maturation, increased CTL infiltration, and facilitated NK cell recruitment, leading to significant inhibition of tumor growth, recurrence, and metastasis. This study presents a novel and practical strategy for developing polymetallic-based anti-tumor immunotherapies.

title: Current Advances in Biomaterials for Glioblastoma Immunotherapy
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) constitutes the most prevalent malignant neoplasm within the central nervous system, representing 12%–15% of intracranial malignant neoplasms. GBM is characterized by molecular heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance, which significantly impair survival prognosis of patients. The current standard treatment regimen involves surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy. Nevertheless, the invasive growth pattern of GBM renders current therapeutic approaches only capable of achieving alleviation of local symptoms and tumor volume reduction, thus impeding the complete eradication of malignant cells and curative efficacy. Biomaterial-enhanced immunotherapy has shown promise as a therapeutic approach owing to its notable therapeutic response rate and favorable safety profile. This therapy effectively impedes tumor progression by precisely modulating the cellular and molecular network of the tumor microenvironment (TME). This review examines the potential mechanisms involved in GBM therapy, with a specific focus on biomaterial-enhanced tumor immunity. Moreover, the review also summarizes immune cell phenotype reprogramming, reversed remodeling of the TME, and the efficacy of synergistic immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) to elicit endogenous antitumor immune responses. Consequently, this in-depth elucidation of synergistic mechanisms between biomaterials and immunotherapy will provide a scientific foundation for the development of a novel generation of immunotherapy regimens for patients with GBM.

title: Correction: Attenuation of osteoarthritis progression via locoregional delivery of Klotho-expressing plasmid DNA and Tanshinon IIA through a stem cell-homing hydrogel
Correction: Delivery of an ERK inhibitor using bioactive lipid nanoparticles reduces angiogenesis and prevents oral squamous cell carcinoma development
Transformable peptide-drug conjugate nanoparticle for bladder cancer therapy
abstract: Bladder cancer (BC) remains a significant health concern, necessitating the development of innovative therapeutic approaches. Herein, a novel strategy is developed utilizing BC cell surface receptor-mediated, transformable peptide nanoparticles, where the prodrug leucine-doxorubicin (Leu-DOX) and the PLZ4 ligand are linked by a β-sheet-forming peptide sequence, KLVFF, to enhance drug delivery efficacy while minimizing toxicity. These transformable peptides self-assemble into nanoparticles with high specificity for BC tissues through the specific recognition of αvβ3 integrin via PLZ4. Upon binding to αvβ3 integrin, the nanoparticles undergo a transformation process facilitated by ligand-receptor interaction, forming nanofibrils on the cancer cell surface, followed by gradual uptake by the cancer cells. In response to matrix metallopeptidase 9 (MMP-9) overexpressed in the tumor microenvironment, the conjugate is cleaved to release the Leu-DOX prodrug, which is subsequently converted into active doxorubicin inside the tumor cells, leading to effective tumor cell elimination. These findings suggest substantial implications for the development of targeted therapies for BC.

title: Aptamer-functionalized exosomal delivery of species-matched Anti-PD-1 antibodies modulates the tumor immune microenvironment during cirrhosis-to-HCC malignant transformation
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) often arises from hepatic cirrhosis, yet interventions that block this malignant transition are lacking. This study developed an aptamer-functionalized exosomal nanoplatform carrying an anti-PD-1 antibody to enable targeted immunomodulation. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of HCC specimens revealed reduced CD8 + T cell infiltration alongside elevated PD-1 expression in CD8 + T cells. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling highlighted suppression of CD8 + T cell-related proteins, upregulation of proteasome 20 S subunit alpha 1 (PSMA1), and enrichment of altered metabolites within lipid metabolic pathways, indicating immune-metabolic dysregulation during cirrhosis-to-HCC progression. The engineered exosomal platform was evaluated in a 3D co-culture system containing HCC cells, cirrhotic hepatocytes, and CD8 + T cells, where it enhanced T cell-associated cytotoxic readouts and reduced fibrosis-related changes. In a mouse model of cirrhosis-associated malignant transformation, the platform showed preferential lesion-associated fluorescence, improved measured liver injury and lesion-burden endpoints, and enhanced CD8 + T cell effector readouts. These findings support exosome/aptamer-assisted anti-PD-1 delivery as a preclinical strategy for immune modulation during cirrhosis-associated malignant transformation, while further validation in human immune-cell systems or humanized models remains necessary.

title: Mechano-immune reinforced exosomes from YAP-activated macrophages counteracting musculoskeletal trauma and age-related decline
abstract: Musculoskeletal repair is jointly constrained by impaired inflammation resolution, elevated oxidative stress, diminished regenerative capacity, and altered mechanical microenvironments. Here, we develop a cell-free reparative strategy based on exosomes derived from YAP-activated M2-like macrophages, integrated with reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive hydrogel delivery. Pharmacological activation of YAP under low-stiffness conditions partially recapitulates the reparative macrophage phenotype induced by matrix stiffening. Exosomes harvested from YAP-activated macrophages (Y-M2-EXO) exhibit stronger anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and pro-regenerative activities than conventional M2 macrophage-derived exosomes (M2-EXO), mitigating oxidative injury and lipid peroxidation-associated cellular damage in mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), preserving mitochondrial homeostasis, and enhancing MSC migration, proliferation, and osteogenic/tenogenic differentiation. MicroRNA sequencing and qRT-PCR validation reveal that YAP activation markedly reshapes the miRNA profile of Y-M2-EXO, enriching a candidate miRNA network associated with inflammatory stress, differentiation and regeneration, senescence homeostasis, and mechano-adaptation, which provides a molecular explanatory framework for the functional superiority of Y-M2-EXO over M2-EXO. To improve local retention and environmentally triggered release, Y-M2-EXO are encapsulated within an ROS-responsive hydrogel dynamically crosslinked by hyaluronic acid-aminophenylboronic acid (HA-APBA) and poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA). In rat models of Achilles tendon rupture and tibial fracture, hydrogel-delivered Y-M2-EXO ameliorate the injured microenvironment, promote structural tissue reconstruction and biomechanical recovery, and maintain robust reparative performance under conditions of restricted mechanical input. In naturally aged mice, Y-M2-EXO reduce the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related inflammatory burden and alleviate bone and muscle degeneration; when combined with aerobic exercise, selected tissue reconstruction and motor function parameters are further improved. Collectively, this study supports donor-cell YAP preprogramming to optimize exosome bioactivity, coupled with ROS-responsive local delivery, as a translationally promising cell-free regulatory strategy for musculoskeletal repair.

title: Supramolecular mRNA-delivering hydrogel for inducing tertiary lymphoid structures and enhancing immunotherapy efficacy
abstract: Background Immune checkpoint blockade has improved cancer treatment outcomes, yet many solid tumors remain immunologically “cold” and resistant to therapy. Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are linked to enhanced survival and response rates, but germinal center-like TLSs are challenging to generate in subcutaneous tumors due to rapid clearance of soluble inductive signals. We engineered an injectable supramolecular hydrogel to co-deliver liposome-formulated mRNAs encoding CXCL13 and LIGHT, thereby stabilizing the complexes and extending intratumoral cytokine production. Results In murine B16.f10, CT26, and 4T1 subcutaneous tumor models, this strategy increased TLS density and maturation, suppressed tumor growth, and prolonged survival. Combination with PD-1 blockade yielded enhanced efficacy antitumor effects, achieving complete tumor regression in some cases. Conclusions Our results support the development of a novel injectable hydrogel-encapsulated formulation in combination with liposomes for enhancing the efficacy of mRNA therapeutics against cancer. title: Aptamer-functionalized GSTK1-derived Super-Mito-EV enable targeted mitochondrial restoration for intervertebral disc repair
abstract: The progression of intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) is accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction and ferroptosis in nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs), highlighting the need for further investigation into mitochondrial homeostasis-related mechanisms and targeted therapeutic strategies. We found that the mitochondrial protein GSTK1 is downregulated in degenerative NPCs, whereas its overexpression partially delays IDD progression in rats. Mechanistically, the GSTK1-ALDH1L2 axis exerts anti-ferroptotic effects by maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis, independently of the classical ACSL4 pathway. GSTK1 also promotes the formation of mitochondria-containing extracellular vesicles through CD38/IP3R/Ca 2+ -associated signaling. Based on these findings, we generated mitochondria-enriched extracellular vesicles derived from GSTK1-overexpressing NPCs (Super-Mito-EV), modified them with EY3 to enhance targeted mitochondrial transfer, and incorporated them into a thermosensitive hydrogel to construct an injectable sustained-release delivery system. In a rat IDD model, this strategy significantly delayed IDD and improved disc structure and molecular homeostasis. In summary, our findings reveal the role of GSTK1–ALDH1L2-mediated mitochondrial homeostasis in IDD-associated ferroptosis and propose a targeted therapeutic strategy based on Super-Mito-EV-mediated mitochondrial delivery.
